editorial:
Set in 1974, this comedy follows a pair of former 1960s radicals who decide to use their old bomb-making skills to chase money and become capitalists. You follow these quirky characters as they scheme, double-cross, and stumble through a world of crime, greed, and bad decisions. The vibe is retro and playful, with a soundtrack and style that throw you right back into the seventies. It feels like a throwback crime comedy where everyone has an angle and nobody can fully trust anyone else. The characters are colorful and a little ridiculous, which keeps things light even when the stakes get dangerous.

The acting is fun and energetic, and the pacing moves quickly enough to keep you engaged without feeling rushed. The humor lands best if you enjoy dry, offbeat comedy and characters who are smarter than they first appear. On the downside, the plot can feel a bit scattered, and some jokes do not land as well as others. Still, if you like retro crime comedies with a twist, this one is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the radicals' big bomb scheme falls apart as betrayals come to light. The money they chased slips away, and the characters who played it straightest end up on top while the schemers get caught in their own traps. The twist reveals that the supposed easy payday was never real, and the radicals are left with nothing but their old skills and a hard lesson about greed. It wraps up with a darkly funny note that fits the seventies crime vibe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves retro crime comedies with quirky characters.
